script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JEN (mid 30s, quirky) and MIKE (late 30s, analytical) sit at a table covered in empty takeout containers. The sun pours in through the window, highlighting their tired faces.

JEN
(sighing)
Another day at the office.

MIKE
(smiling)
You say that every day.

Jen rolls her eyes, a small smile playing on her lips.

JEN
I know. But it's true.

MIKE
Well, at least we have each other.

They share a moment of genuine warmth before Jen's phone rings. She answers, her expression instantly falling.

JEN
(into phone)
Yes, I'll be there in 10 minutes.

MIKE
What's wrong?

JEN
(sighs)
My boss wants me to come in on my day off.

MIKE
(concerned)
Do you need me to go with you?

Jen shakes her head.

JEN
No, it's fine. I'll handle it.

Mike nods, understanding the look of resignation on her face.

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - DAY

Jen enters the building, her spirits dragging. As she passes a row of cubicles, MIKE (off-screen) calls out to her.

MIKE
(off-screen)
Hey, you forgot your lunch.

Jen turns around, her eyes brightening at the sight of a brown bag in Mike's hand.

JEN
(grateful)
Thanks, Mike. You're a lifesaver.

INT. BOSSES OFFICE - DAY

Jen stands before her boss, MR. JOHNSON (late 50s, stern), a look of apprehension on her face.

MR. JOHNSON
Jen, I need you to work on this project. I know it's your day off, but it's important.

Jen opens her mouth to protest but then reconsiders.

JEN
Okay, I'll do it.

MR. JOHNSON
(pleased)
Excellent. I knew I could count on you.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Jen and Mike sit across from each other, their hands wrapped around steaming mugs.

JEN
(sighing)
I can't believe I let him make me come in on my day off.

MIKE
(sympathetic)
I know it's not fair. But at least you have a job.

JEN
(smiling)
I guess you're right. And at least I have you to make sure I eat.

They share a laugh as they sip their coffee.

INT. PARK - DAY

Jen and Mike sit on a bench, basking in the sunlight. Jen pulls out a sketchpad and begins to draw, while Mike watches, a small smile playing on his lips.

JEN
(looking up)
I've always loved drawing in the park. It's so peaceful.

MIKE
(agrees)
It's one of the things I love about you.

They share a tender moment, their hands brushing as they lean closer together.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jen and Mike sit at their table, covered in takeout containers and drawing supplies. They laugh and talk as they work on their projects, their friendship shining through.

JEN
(looking up)
I'm glad I have you, Mike.

MIKE
(smiling)
And I'm glad I have you, Jen.

They share a look, their eyes locking in a silent promise to always be there for each other, no matter what.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
